attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his co-authored post, stated in the authors' voice.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense observation that current approaches still struggle with role-reversing reorderings. Faithful to the statement.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: substantial, repeatable difficulty in representative contemporary systems, not failure on every example. Using the 2022 period up to publication is reasonable.

evidence.note: Winoground (April 2022) tests controlled caption pairs with the same words in different orders. All contemporary vision-language models scored below chance on the group score. This is directly on point and inside the period.
A later (Nov 2022) analysis of Winoground. It says the failures are meaningful but traces them to vision-language fusion. That bears on cause, not on whether the problem existed.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous controlled evidence (Winoground) shows representative models failing systematically when swapped word order changes the meaning. That meets the support condition. The later analysis qualifies the cause but confirms the failures are real. The evidence covers vision-language models rather than every approach, but the claim does not require universality.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his co-authored post.

semantics.note: Faithful in substance, but 'all of this literature' is hyperbolic. In context, 'approach' refers to the method of building systems by predicting word sequences.

contract.note: The contract widens 'the LLM approach' to all research about LLMs, so probing studies count as the approach engaging the literature. In context the speaker means the model-building method. That widening stretches the claim against him, and the result turns on it.

evidence.note: A 2021 probing paper that uses dynamic semantics to analyse BART and T5. It shows some LLM-adjacent research engaged the literature. It does not show the model-building approach drew on it.

reviews.rationale: The one contradiction rests on counting interpretability research as 'the LLM approach', which the speaker's context does not support. Read fairly, as the method of building systems from next-word prediction, the claim is not settled by the packet. The packet itself notes it has nothing on how architecture or training decisions were made.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his co-authored post, listing consequences in the authors' voice.

semantics.note: The statement says inadequate attention to the three factors has consequences, including (b). It is a causal claim, and the normalisation preserves it.

contract.note: It is reasonable to require controlled evidence that links the factors to truth discrimination. Treating inadequate attention as missing capabilities in the models is a minor reframing.

evidence.note: TruthfulQA shows contemporary models giving false answers. It does not test the proposed causes.
GopherCite's evidence grounding did not improve truthfulness. That limits grounding as a fix but neither tests nor refutes the three-factor causal claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows LLMs had difficulty with truthfulness, but nothing manipulates reference, cognitive models or compositionality to show a causal effect. Nothing rules one out either. Under the contract the causal claim stays unsettled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his co-authored post.

semantics.note: 'Don't really' sets a threshold of substantive, human-like model building for narratives and the world. 'Current AI systems' in this essay means the prevailing systems, chiefly LLMs. The proposition keeps the gist but loses that scope.

contract.note: The contract takes 'current AI systems' to cover any earlier research system and treats any limited functional state tracking, such as toy bAbI stories or control-task latents, as a contradiction. That ignores 'really' and the narrative context, which stretches the claim against the speaker.

evidence.note: EntNet (2017) tracks entity states in simplified stories. It is a research prototype, not a prevailing current system, and shows no substantive story comprehension.
A Google company disclosure (2020) describing Dreamer's latent world model for control tasks. It is a limited functional model outside the essay's focus on language and narrative.

reviews.rationale: The contradictions come from reading 'current AI systems' as any system and 'cognitive model' as any functional state tracking. On a fair reading, that prevailing systems such as LLMs did not substantively build such models, the packet has no evidence about those systems. The claim is therefore not settled.
